problem: A particle $P$ of mass $2\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a resultant force. The particle's acceleration is $(3{t}^{2}+4)\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=1\,m/s$ when $t=0\,s,$ calculate the work done by the force between the times $t=1\,s$ and $t=2\,s.$

feedback.problem: A particle $P$ of mass $2\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a resultant force. The particle's velocity is $2t\,m/s,$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the work done by the force between the times $t=1\,s$ and $t=2\,s.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The work-energy principle states that the work done by a resultant force on a particle equals the change in the particle's kinetic energy. That is,

$$
W=Δ\,\text{KE}
$$

where the change in kinetic energy of a particle is given by

$$
Δ\,\text{KE}=\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2}
$$

and $m$ is the particle's mass, ${v}_{0}$ is its initial velocity, and ${v}_{1}$ is its final velocity.

The particle's velocity is given by $v(t)=2t,$ where $t$ is time in seconds. So, the particle's initial velocity, at $t=1$, is

$$
{v}_{0}=v(1)=2(1)=2\,m/s,
$$

and final velocity, at $t=2$, is

$$
{v}_{1}=v(2)=2(2)=4\,m/s.
$$

Therefore, by the work-energy principle, the work done by the force between these times is

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =Δ\,\text{KE} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot (4)^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot (2)^{2} \\  & =16-4 \\  & =12\,J.\end{aligned}
$$
